items.summary: CTO review: approve containment-only disposition. Retain the three control-plane specifications as deferred backlog; do not create change requests, requeues, deployments, dependencies, telemetry, spend, or site edits. The concepts are technically feasible and reversible, but implementation must wait until existing failure repair-or-close, isolation, validation, rollback, deduplication, measurement, and financial-containment gates are complete.

The safest future implementation order is: failure-aware queue lifecycle first, approval-to-execution reconciliation second, measurement-readiness gating third. Each must run in an isolated control-plane worktree with fixture-only tests, no production credentials, no site-repository writes, no external calls, and explicit rollback. Existing records are the only permitted evidence source until a separately approved measurement design exists.

Queue eligibility remains false this cycle. Existing evidence shows 47 open failure follow-ups, 9 failed implementation requests, 28 deployed improvements awaiting measurement, and only 2 proven outcomes. Preserve the deferred opportunities and continue only existing repair-or-close, period-aligned attribution reconciliation, and bounded read-only legal/security evidence.
